task: Add a role-gated "Create user" button and modal to the CodeMie UI Users Management page that calls the existing backend POST /v1/admin/users endpoint.

key_reasoning.reason: Task description is directionally clear (button, modal, existing POST /v1/admin/users), but technical-analysis.md documents four unresolved design decisions: no existing password-field pattern to imitate, the ticket says 'checkboxes' while the closest analog (UserDetailsPopup) uses Switch for the same three role flags, whether the button/form should also gate on getIdpProvider()==='local' (backend 400s otherwise) is unconfirmed, and whether the edit-flow's role-interdependency rules (maintainer implies admin; admin/maintainer clears auditor) should carry over to create is undecided.

Base risk is low — a near-identical modal+form template exists (ChangeRolePopup.tsx: Popup + react-hook-form + yup + Controller calling a userStore method) and every userStore admin method shares one call shape. Bumped to L because the new work is security-sensitive in a way the precedent does not cover: this form creates local accounts with privilege flags (is_admin/is_maintainer/is_auditor) and a password field, and the codebase has zero existing password-input pattern (masking, min-length feedback, visibility toggle) and zero test coverage for any create-flow to extend.

Three components change, mostly within one clear pattern: UsersManagementPage.tsx (add role-gated button), a new popup component under usersManagement/components/popups/ (following the ChangeRolePopup template), and src/store/user.ts (one new method matching the uniform api.post(...).then(r.json()).catch(toaster.error+throw) shape already used by every other admin method there). Effectively 2 layers (UI, Store/Service) with a well-established pattern, not new abstractions.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: user creation introduces a secret-handling surface (password field) and privilege-assignment flags (is_admin/is_maintainer) with no existing reusable pattern for either in this codebase.
